reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order list against the refunds W2 reported as applied, so I don't pay out on a mismatch.
W2 reported three refunds as applied. I'll check the shared refund ledger to confirm they match before computing any balances.

The refund ledger matches W2's report exactly: orders 102, 103, and 105 all have matching amounts, and no refund exceeds its order. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 42714 matches my own check: orders 100 and 103 total 46215, minus the 3501 refund on order 103. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 65068 matches my check: orders 101 and 104 total 65068 with no refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 2634 matches my check: orders 102 and 105 total 38498, minus refunds 2289 and 33575 (35864), leaves 2634. All three balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 42714 is recorded and matches its verified balance. Birch's verified balance is 65068, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's verified balance is 2634. Recording cobalt's payout is the last step.
All three customers have been paid their verified net balances, and each record_payout returned ok. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
